system_overview: This specification models an asynchronous Byzantine consensus protocol for reliable broadcast, based on the algorithm in Figure 3 of Bracha and Toueg's 1985 paper. The protocol allows a set of processes to reach agreement on a binary value despite the presence of Byzantine (arbitrarily faulty) processes. It uses a three-phase approach with ECHO and READY message rounds to ensure that correct processes can reliably agree.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes. Each process is either correct or Byzantine. Byzantine processes can behave arbitrarily, including sending spurious messages. The protocol tolerates up to T Byzantine faults out of N total processes, with the constraint that N must exceed 3T. Up to F processes may actually become faulty in a given execution, where F is at most T.
state_variables: The system tracks: the total number of ECHO messages sent by all processes, the total number of READY messages sent by all processes, the number of ECHO messages received by each individual process, the number of READY messages received by each individual process, the current number of Byzantine processes, and the control location of each process (which indicates whether it has proposed a value, sent an ECHO, sent a READY, accepted, or become Byzantine).
initial_state: Initially, no ECHO or READY messages have been sent. No process has received any messages. No process is Byzantine. Each process starts in one of two proposal states representing its initial proposed value (either 0 or 1). Two special initial configurations are also defined: one where all processes propose 0, and one where all processes propose 1.
actions: The protocol supports the following transitions: (1) A process that has not yet become faulty and is still in its initial proposal state may become Byzantine, incrementing the Byzantine count, up to the fault bound F. (2) A process may receive an ECHO or READY message, incrementing its received count for the corresponding message type. When receiving, messages from both correct senders and Byzantine senders may be included. (3) A process that proposed value 1 sends an ECHO message. A process that proposed value 0 may also send an ECHO if it has received enough ECHO messages (at least the floor of (N+T+2)/2) or enough READY messages (at least T+1). (4) A process that has already sent an ECHO and has received enough ECHO messages (at least (N+T+2)/2) or enough READY messages (at least T+1) sends a READY message. (5) A process that has sent a READY message and has received at least 2T+1 READY messages decides (accepts).
safety_properties: Unforgeability: if all processes initially propose 0, then no process ever accepts. Agreement: if any process accepts, then eventually all correct processes accept or are Byzantine.
liveness_properties: Correctness: if all processes initially propose 1, then eventually some process accepts. Agreement as a liveness property: if any process accepts at any point, then eventually every correct (non-Byzantine) process also accepts.
model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Control locations are six distinct states representing the two proposal values, echo-sent, ready-sent, accepted, and Byzantine.
additional_assumptions: The model uses a message-counting abstraction rather than tracking individual messages, since all messages are of the same type. Weak fairness is assumed on the actions of correct processes (receiving, sending echo, sending ready, and deciding), ensuring progress when actions are continuously enabled. The specification requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0.
